children: Shares of online vehicle auction company Copart

jumped 3.3% in the morning session after JPMorgan analyst Jash Patwa upgraded the stock from Neutral to Overweight and raised its price target from $32.00 to $40.00, as reported by CNBC. The upgrade reflects a more bullish stance from the investment bank, shifting its outlook from a neutral view to one anticipating outperformance. The raised price target from $32.00 to $40.00 points to increased upside potential for the company's shares. Positive rating revisions and higher price targets from major Wall Street institutions frequently boost investor sentiment and drive buying interest in the stock.
The shares were trading at $33.37, up 3.8% from the previous close.
What Is The Market Telling Us

Copart’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 5 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 15 days ago when the stock gained 6.1% on the news that Bloomberg reported the online auto auction company is among suitors for car-insurance software firm CCC Intelligent Solutions. According to Bloomberg, Dallas-based Copart is competing with private-equity firms including GTCR and Veritas Capital, that talks are ongoing, and that no deal is certain.

CCC has been exploring options with an adviser after Elliott Investment Management built a large stake. A deal would push Copart deeper into the insurance claims and repair workflow that feeds salvage volume. Bloomberg said CCC jumped as much as 14% on August 18th and closed up 6.7%; treat this as rumor-stage M&A, not a signed transaction.

Copart is down 11.7% since the beginning of the year, and at $33.37 per share, it is trading 33.2% below its 52-week high of $49.97 from September 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Copart’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $916.46.
